summary.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for first time (INR101 crore, 10% margin), revenue up 29% YoY on export-led pricing.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 29% YoY, driven mainly by cables and wire export volumes and realisations, with EBITDA up 27% YoY to a 10% margin and PAT of about INR64 crore (up 22% YoY). Management attributed the strong quarter largely to pass-through of higher raw material prices and a war-risk/volatility premium on exports, mainly to MENA. Volumes grew only about 1% YoY, and average utilisation fell to around 66% as the new 48,000 t Bhiwadi XLPE plant started up in April 2026. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% volume growth and 13-14% revenue growth, and announced a phased entry into BESS with a 6-8% initial EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.value: INR100+ crore (about INR101 crore per analyst recap), first time above INR100 crore
About INR19.6/kg as cited by management (vs normal INR15-17)
financial_highlights.change: Up in absolute terms; margin % lower

financial_highlights.value: About INR300-plus crore in the quarter, mainly MENA

segments.name: Cables and wire (export)
segments.commentary: Main driver of the quarter, with about INR300-plus crore of export revenue, mainly MENA, at better prices than competitors. Volumes rose only a few percent in export; value gains came from pricing and war-risk premiums.

segments.name: Domestic compounds
segments.commentary: Local demand softened in Q1 because of high prices, with volume growth around 1% for the quarter overall. Management expects volume to recover as price uncertainty eases.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: New vertical starting with a supply model, with an expected 6-8% EBITDA margin, rising toward 11-15% long term with EPC and system integrator models. Phase 1 is about 1 GW / 1 GWh with INR150-200 crore capex plus working capital, and the timeline has slipped by a couple of quarters due to a West-to-East shift.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target of about 15% (2,31,000 t for the year; about 60,000 t per quarter needed in Q2-Q4), with the Bhiwadi plant ramping to about 50% average utilisation.
FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 13-14%, built on FY26 average realisation of about INR145/kg with no price increase assumed; management says guidance will be surpassed given Q1.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 10-12% (INR16-17/kg); Q1 margin of INR19.6/kg not expected to be sustained every quarter.
Top-line ambition of INR5,000 crore by FY30.
Bhiwadi plant expected to add incremental revenue of about INR500-odd crore at full utilisation; about INR200-250 crore in FY27 at 50% utilisation.
Committed FY27 investment of INR150-175 crore, covering MV capacity in East, HFFR expansion to 20,000 t, a new Vapi site and BESS.
Cash conversion cycle expected to normalise to 55-60 days; finance costs expected to ease from July.
Resin prices expected to take 3-6 months to return to pre-war levels once Hormuz situation clears.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 3,16,400 t per annum as of June 2026; about 3,34,400 t by year end after additions.
Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) greenfield XLPE plant of 48,000 t commissioned April 2026, lifting XLPE capacity to 2,14,500 t; running at about 20-25% currently, targeting 50% average utilisation in FY27.
Capex incurred so far is about INR77 crore; FY27 committed investment is INR150-175 crore.
HFFR capacity to be expanded to 20,000 t as targeted for FY27; new Vapi site to consolidate products; MV cable capability being built in East (completion by end FY27 or Q1).

BESS phase 1 about 1 GW / 1 GWh with INR150-200 crore capex plus working capital, funded from internal accruals; 1 GW target around mid-FY29; the site is shifting from West to East (Bengal under consideration pending state incentive policy expected by end August).
demand_pricing: Export pricing benefited from war-related volatility; the company charged a risk premium on export quotes, and raw material prices changed weekly or more often in March-April.
Analysts were told that prices eased slightly in July, so the Q2 export number of about INR300 crore may be lower in realisation even if volumes hold.
Order books are largely spot, covering about 10-20 days; management can only give visibility up to August.
Customer product approvals carry over to the new Bhiwadi plant, with no new approvals needed.
Bhiwadi plant to serve existing customers in Rajasthan and Delhi, with some West capacity redirected to Europe and indirectly to the US; management sees opportunity to take share from imports.
Water tree retardant XLPE is an approved product sold in volume, not a new launch; management says the EU FTA gives direct benefit on existing European customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise in absolute terms while the percentage margin fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports to MENA earned better prices than competitors, with volumes up only single digits; the EBITDA per ton was about INR19.6, versus a normal range of about INR15-17. It stated that margin is mostly pass-through and the percentage margin of 10% is still healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: The first phase is a supply model with a 6-8% EBITDA margin, rising by 2-3% per stage as EPC and system integrator models are added, toward a long-term 11-15%. BOO/BOOT are not planned for now. Phase 1 is expected to cost INR150-200 crore including working capital, funded from internal accruals, with the timeline delayed by a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance only 13% revenue growth when capacity rises 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance uses FY26 average realisation of about INR145/kg with no price increase. Volume growth of 15% is the key metric, with Bhiwadi ramping to about 50% utilisation. Management said guidance will be exceeded given Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 outlook and how far does the export number hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the INR300 crore export figure lower because prices eased in July. Volumes in Q2 are expected to be better than Q1, though the exact value may be lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise and what is the cash conversion cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher finance cost came from working capital borrowing after the March raw material price spike raised inventory and debtors. It has eased from July. Cash conversion cycle rose in Q1 and is expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share given raw material volatility and import disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said it expects share gains in medium-voltage XLPE, where its share is lower, and that supply disruption is pushing local customers toward domestic suppliers. Bhiwadi will serve existing customers only, mainly in Rajasthan and Delhi.

risks_watch: Export margins depend on war and freight volatility (Hormuz); management says the premium will shrink and the next quarter may be lower.
Volume growth was only about 1% in Q1 against a 15% full-year target, requiring about 60,000 t per quarter from Q2.
Bhiwadi utilisation at 20-25% currently against a 50% FY27 assumption; the ramp-up is the key swing factor for revenue.
BESS timeline slipped by a couple of quarters due to the West-to-East relocation, pending the Bengal incentive policy; the company is still choosing a site and has no clear margin track record yet.
Working capital and finance costs rose in Q1; cash conversion cycle needs to return to 55-60 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural demand and on hitting full-year guidance, but cautious on near-term pricing and on the BESS timeline. Management declined to give visibility beyond August, citing spot-driven order books and Middle East uncertainty.
key_quotes: So rather we have used the time and we have shifted to a better base.
It is mainly pass-on business. We are a transparent supplier to most of the customers we have.
We are confident of achieving 15% volume growth this year despite the first quarter being low on the growth having just 1% growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on structural demand, full-year volume and revenue guidance, and the INR5,000 crore FY30 ambition, but cautious on near-term export pricing, Q2 realisations, the Bhiwadi ramp and the BESS timeline; analysts probed the margin per ton, the 13% guide against 25% capacity growth
